text: The Harborline project wasn't just practice — it's now your best interview material. This lesson covers the questions a cross-platform DBA role is actually likely to ask, and how to answer them using the specific work you just did.

Expect architecture questions. On Oracle, be ready to explain that instance and database are genuinely separate concepts, not synonyms. On MySQL, explain pluggable storage engines like InnoDB versus MyISAM. On PostgreSQL, explain why a company would actually choose it for new analytics work — cost and its extension ecosystem, not trend-chasing.

Expect migration questions too. Chapter 17 gave you an assessment-first framework: scope the project first, walk through the platform's key differences like T-SQL versus PL/pgSQL, and only then talk tooling and data type mapping. That sequence shows judgment, not memorized commands.

When asked to describe a time you tuned a slow query, tell the actual Lesson 94 Oracle story: a reporting query that grew from under a minute to twenty minutes, traced through AWR to a missing index and stale statistics, fixed and verified with an execution plan. Specific, with a before-and-after number.
You now have real technical reasoning to back up every answer. Next up, Lesson 96: wrapping up this course and this path, and where to head next.
